problems.title: The prefix quantity is residual prior entropy mass, not conditional Shannon entropy
problems.source_location: Section 3.1, Eqs. (4)–(5), PDF p. 4; released code/trie.py, lines 39–61 and compute_information_gain from line 126.
claim: Section 3.1, Eqs. (4)–(5), PDF p. 4, interprets a prefix score as Shannon uncertainty and its parent-minus-child difference as information gain. The displayed \(R_s\) sums fixed prior terms \(-p_i\log p_i\) over compatible items without conditional renormalization. Released code/trie.py, lines 39–61 and compute_information_gain from line 126, implements that same prior-mass sum.
analysis: For prior \((0.8,0.1,0.1)\), a prefix retaining the last two items gives posterior \((0.5,0.5)\). Its entropy is \(\log2\approx0.6931\), greater than the original \(0.6390\), but removing the first item's contribution produces a positive declared gain. If the retained mass is \(M\) and its normalized entropy is \(H\), the implemented residual is \(MH-M\log M\), not \(H\). The score remains a definable heuristic, with a different information-theoretic interpretation.
result: The normalized-entropy interpretation fails, but the implemented pruning score has a coherent unchanged interpretation and no recommendation-accuracy refutation follows.
repair: Describe the unchanged quantity as residual prior entropy mass, or separately define and evaluate a conditionally normalized entropy score. These alternatives are different scoring rules.
problems.impact_rationale: The normalized-entropy interpretation fails, but the implemented pruning score has a coherent unchanged interpretation and no recommendation-accuracy refutation follows.

problems.title: Converting item-ID frequencies to title frequencies overwrites collisions
problems.source_location: Released code/compute_item_freq.py, load_item_titles, lines 9–29, and count_item_frequencies, lines 32–56.
claim: This is a released-code correctness finding, not an assertion that the paper contains a theorem about duplicate titles. In code/compute_item_freq.py, load_item_titles, lines 9–29, accepts a tab-separated title followed by an integer item ID. count_item_frequencies, lines 32–56, counts interaction rows by item ID and converts that counter to a dictionary keyed by title.
analysis: Two item IDs have frequencies \(5\) and \(7\) but share a title; a third title has frequency \(11\). Repeated title-key assignment overwrites the first frequency, producing total \(18\) instead of \(23\). Summing colliding frequencies restores title-level mass; keeping distinct item identities requires retaining an identifier.
result: Conditional preprocessing defect; its exposure in the actual benchmarks was not established.
repair: For title-level aggregation, add frequencies on title collisions rather than overwriting them. If item identity matters, preserve the separate item ID as well.
problems.impact_rationale: The routine loses count mass on accepted duplicate-title inputs; collisions reaching the published benchmark pipeline remain unestablished.
problems.existing_correction_status: A local correction or qualification is proposed where specified; author adoption is not established.

impact_rationale: The latest version retains a local entropy interpretation error and conditional frequency-preparation defect. The unchanged score remains a usable heuristic and empirical recommendation comparisons are not adjudicated.
